definitions.explanation: A very polite and humble way to acknowledge a request or instruction, commonly used by service staff. The most formal alternative to わかりました.

examples.japanese: 「{窓側|まどがわ}の{席|せき}をお{願|ねが}いします。」「かしこまりました。」
「お{水|みず}をもう{一|いっ}{杯|ぱい}いただけますか。」「かしこまりました。{少々|しょうしょう}お{待|ま}ちください。」
examples.english: "Could I have another glass of water?" "Certainly. Please wait a moment."

examples.japanese: 「{予約|よやく}を{来週|らいしゅう}の{金曜日|きんようび}に{変更|へんこう}したいのですが。」「かしこまりました。{確認|かくにん}いたします。」
examples.english: "I'd like to change my reservation to next Friday." "Certainly. Let me confirm that for you."

notes:
The past tense of かしこまる (to be humbled, to respectfully acknowledge), used as a set phrase. One of the most formal acknowledgment expressions in Japanese.

USAGE:
Primarily used by people in service roles — hotel staff, restaurant servers, shop clerks, customer service representatives. It signals both understanding and willingness to comply with a polite, respectful tone. Not typically used between equals or in casual settings.

FORMALITY SCALE:
- {分|わ}かった — understood (casual)
- {分|わ}かりました — understood (polite)
- {承知|しょうち}しました — understood (formal/business)
- かしこまりました — certainly (most formal/humble)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {承知|しょうち}しました — understood; formal business acknowledgment, slightly less humble
- {了解|りょうかい}しました — roger, understood; common but considered less formal
- {分|わ}かりました — understood; standard polite acknowledgment
